$comment: One entry per English string: which screens it appears on, what it means, and what each placeholder carries. English is canonical -- a translation is checked against the English, and this against the app.

%@ could not open your drives.context: Title of the permission screen when drives that were set to reopen after a restart could not be opened. States a fact; it is not an apology.

%@ does not yet support writing to this.context: Under the title of the blue note about an image format that is only ever read.

%@ free of %@.context: Free space on an open drive: how much is free, of how much there is. Both are already formatted sizes such as 12,4 GB.

%@ has been removed.context: Title shown when uninstalling has finished.

%@ image can only be opened read-only.context: Title of that note. The placeholder is a format name such as VHDX and is never translated.

%@ is free software under the GPL, versi.context: The licence paragraph in the help sheet. Legal wording: keep it exact. GPL and anylinuxfs are names.

%@ is not able to open this file format..context: The title of every refusal to open a disk image. One title for all of them; the sentence under it says which reason applies.

%@ is still new. The Linux tools and dri.context: The whole of the first-launch notice. Says the app is early, that reading and copying off a drive is the safe use, and that writing should be treated as experimental. Plain and calm; it is not a warning dialog and there is nothing to decide. The only button says OK.

%@ opens BitLocker, Linux and virtual ma.context: The welcome paragraph, in two parts separated by a blank line. The first says what the app is for; the second says why a permission has to be granted by hand rather than asked for. Raw device level means reading the disk directly rather than its files.

%@ opens in the background when you log.context: The explanation under the setting for reopening drives after a restart.

%@ starts a small Linux virtual machine,.context: The paragraph explaining how the app works. The last two sentences are deliberately short.

%@ will be moved to the Bin..context: A line in the uninstall confirmation, listing what will happen. Bin is Apple's word in British English; use Apple's word in this language.

%lld drives had stopped responding and w.context: A notice after several drives went away at once. Needs the plural forms of this language.

%lld drives or images are open. You can.context: Warning across the top of the drive list, and of the unlock and failure screens, when as many drives are open as this Mac can serve at once. Every drive is served over a network connection to this Mac, and there are only so many addresses to serve them on. Drives and disk images count alike.

placeholders.is: how many drives and images are open
how many can be open at once, twelve on most Macs

%lld open drives will be ejected..context: Another line in that list. Needs the plural forms of this language.

%lld percent.context: Progress while the Linux environment is unpacked. The number is a percentage from 0 to 100.

%lld volumes.context: A count of volumes inside one container, shown on a row. Needs the plural forms of this language.

%lld volumes are open on this Mac alread.context: Shown when this copy of the app has nothing open but the Mac's capacity is already spoken for -- another copy of the app, or a test harness driving the engine, is serving volumes. The first number is how many are open on the machine, the second the most that can be served at once. It replaces the 'eject one to open another' sentence, which asked for an ejection of something the person cannot see in this window.

260 MB of disk: 160 MB for the app, 100.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of requirements. A fragment: no full stop.

30 MB of RAM per open drive sitting idle.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of requirements. A fragment: no full stop.

A VHDX that was not shut down cleanly. O.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app cannot open. A fragment: no full stop.

A crash report was found.context: Title of a note in the report sheet when macOS left a crash log.

A drive %@ can open..context: A row in the disk list for a drive this app can open. The counterpart of the lines that say why another one cannot be; what the volume may hold is in the subtitle above it already.

A drive that refuses to be written to is.context: A bullet under Opening read-only in the help sheet. A fragment, not a sentence: no full stop.

A macOS system volume..context: A row in the disk list: this volume belongs to the running system and is shown but never offered.

About %@.context: Menu item. Opens the help sheet.

About & Help.context: The name of that menu item's group.

Administrator password.context: Row title in the permissions panel. The permission is to act as an administrator, not a password to type here.

Administrator password: asked for once w.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of permissions.

All Drives.context: Button. Goes back to the list of drives, leaving this one open.

Allow %@ in the window that just opened,.context: Shown after switching that setting on, while macOS asks for approval.

Also delete %lld saved passphrases (%@).context: A checkbox in the uninstall confirmation. Needs plural forms; the bracketed part lists the drives.

An Apple Silicon Mac. Intel Macs are not.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of requirements. A fragment: no full stop. Apple Silicon and Intel are Apple's own words.

An exFAT image is handed to macOS, which.context: A bullet under Opening a disk image in the help sheet.

An issue on GitHub is answered sooner. S.context: Under the two buttons at the foot of the report sheet. Says which route is faster and when to prefer the other. GitHub is a product name.

Another drive is open, and the drive eng.context: A failure sentence. After the engine changes, the first run has to be the only one; several drives can be open together again afterwards.

Appearance.context: Settings section: light, dark or system.

Appears only while a drive is unlocked,.context: Explanation under the menu bar setting.

Approve.context: Button on that row when a background item is waiting to be approved in Login Items.

Asked each time.context: Status on that row when there is no background helper, so macOS asks for authorisation at every mount.

Author.context: A row label in the help sheet's About section.

Back.context: Button. Returns to the screen the reader came from, which is the passphrase field for this drive rather than the list of drives.

BitLocker drives, unlocked with the volu.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app can open. A fragment, not a sentence: no full stop.

Cancel.context: Button that abandons a dialogue. The standard macOS word.

Caps Lock is on.context: Warning beside the passphrase field. Caps Lock is the key's name on the keyboard.

Check Now.context: Button. Checks for an update immediately.

Check for Updates….context: Menu item. Ends with an ellipsis character because a dialogue follows.

Checking every disk….context: Shown while the survey runs. Ends with an ellipsis character, not three dots.

Checking this drive for damage.context: A step in the list shown while a drive is opening, alongside "Unlocking and mounting". It appears only on a drive that turned out to be damaged, and it is the step somebody waits on: the check reads the whole file table, about a minute on a 250 GB drive. Present tense, the same form as the other steps.

Choose File → Open Disk Image, or File →.context: A bullet naming two menu items. The arrows mean: then choose. In a right-to-left language they point the other way.

Choose a disk image or container file to.context: The prompt in the file chooser opened by File → Open Disk Image.

Click + at the bottom of the list, selec.context: Step 2 of three. The + is a button at the bottom-left of the Full Disk Access list; Applications is the folder, by Apple's name for it in this language.

Come back to this window and click Relau.context: Step 3 of three. Relaunch is the button on this same screen and must be called exactly what that button is called.

Connect the drive and choose Rescan. If.context: Shown when nothing was found. Names the Rescan button and the File menu item. The arrow means: then choose.

Copied.context: Confirmation shown for a moment after the report was copied.

Copy Details.context: Button. Puts the whole report on the clipboard.

Deleting %lld saved passphrases.context: A step while uninstalling. Needs the plural forms of this language.

Deleting the Linux environment.context: A step while uninstalling: the unpacked Linux system is removed.

Details that will be included.context: Heading above the report itself. The point is that nothing is sent unseen.

Disk Image.context: Shown in a row's subtitle where a physical drive would say USB. Means the row is a file, not hardware.

Dismiss.context: The label of the small × that closes a passing message, such as a drive having stopped responding. Read aloud by a screen reader and shown as a tooltip; the button itself is the × symbol. Apple's own word for this control in this language.

Done.context: Button that closes the help sheet.

Download and install them.context: The second half of the updates setting: not only check, but install.

Drives sealed to a TPM rather than a pas.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app cannot open. A fragment: no full stop. TPM is a hardware chip and keeps its acronym.

Early Development.context: Title of the sheet shown once, on the first launch, as soon as the drive list is up. Two words, a heading rather than a sentence.

Eject.context: Button on an open drive's row, and in the menu bar. Ejecting is what macOS calls unmounting safely.

Eject %@.context: Menu item in the status menu, one per open drive.

Eject It and Open.context: Button on the failure screen, shown only when the drive could not be opened because macOS has it mounted already. It unmounts the drive from macOS and opens it here, in one step. Title case, as macOS button labels are. 'Eject' should be the word this language's Finder uses for ejecting a disk.

Eject a drive or an image before opening.context: Shown in the File menu under the two greyed-out items for opening a drive or a disk image, saying why they cannot be used. Not a button.

Eject and Quit.context: Button in the dialogue shown when quitting with drives open, and the status menu's own quit item while a drive is open. The same words in both places, for the same act.

Eject it in Finder when you are finished.context: Last line of the sheet that reports macOS opened an image itself. The app is not holding it, so the app cannot eject it.

Ejecting %@.context: Read aloud while a drive is being ejected.

Ejecting %lld open drives.context: A step while uninstalling. Needs the plural forms of this language.

Ejecting….context: Shown on the row while it happens. Ends with an ellipsis character.

Engine output.context: Read aloud as the name of the block holding the engine's own text.

Enter the drive's passphrase..context: Said by a screen reader when the unlock screen appears for a Linux drive.

Enter the drive's password, or its 48-di.context: The same for a BitLocker drive.

Every drive and image can be opened read.context: A bullet under Opening read-only. Names the Open and Unlock buttons.

Every drive attached to this Mac, whethe.context: Subtitle of the sheet. Says why disks appear that cannot be opened.

Everything else was removed. %@ itself c.context: Shown when everything was removed except the app. Bin is what macOS calls it in British English; use Apple's word in this language.

Examining its contents..context: Under the title while a disk image is being opened, which takes a moment.

External.context: Part of a row's subtitle: the drive is plugged in rather than built in.

FileVault and encrypted disk images, whi.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app cannot open. A fragment: no full stop. FileVault is Apple's own encryption.

Forget.context: Button. Discards the passphrase saved in the Keychain for this drive.

Full Disk Access.context: Row title in the permissions panel, and the name macOS gives the permission.

Full Disk Access: macOS will not let any.context: A bullet in the permissions list.

GNU General Public License.context: The licence's name, in the About section. Never translated: an unofficial translation of a licence name is not the licence.

Granted permission will only apply once.context: The note under step 3, in grey. Explains why relaunching is part of the instructions rather than an afterthought.

Group %lld of the recovery key is not va.context: Shown when a BitLocker recovery key has 48 digits but one group of six fails the checksum Windows uses, which usually means those six were mistyped. The placeholder is which group, counting from 1.
placeholders: which group of six, counting from 1

Handing the drive to Finder.context: The last step of opening a drive: the mount is being handed to macOS so it appears in Finder. A step name in a list, present participle.

Hide.context: Tooltip on the eye button while the typed passphrase is visible.

Hide Menu Bar Icon.context: Item in the status menu that takes the icon out of the menu bar. The same setting as the Settings toggle “Show %@ in the menu bar”, offered where somebody who wants the icon gone is already looking. An instruction, not a question.

Hide the credential.context: Read aloud for that button in the same state.

How %@ works, and what it supports.context: Tooltip on the help button in the header.

How it works.context: A section heading in the help sheet.

If it is already in the list, switch it.context: The note under step 2, in grey. Covers the case where the app is already listed, which happens after a reinstall.

Images that name another file: a VMware.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app cannot open. A fragment: no full stop. The reason is deliberate: an image that names other files chooses what gets read.

Internal.context: Part of a row's subtitle: the drive is inside the Mac.

It is in the Bin. Nothing else of it is.context: Under the title when uninstalling finished cleanly.

LUKS drives from Linux, both LUKS1 and L.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app can open. A fragment, not a sentence: no full stop.

LUKS volumes whose header is stored sepa.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app cannot open. A fragment: no full stop.

LVM inside LUKS, as Ubuntu, Debian, Mint.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app can open. A fragment, not a sentence: no full stop. The distribution names are proper nouns.

Language.context: Settings section for the interface language.

Last checked: %@.context: Under the update buttons. The placeholder is a date and time formatted by macOS.

Leave Open.context: The other button in that dialogue: quit without ejecting.

Lets %@ read the encrypted data itself..context: The explanation on the Full Disk Access row.

Licence.context: A section heading in the help sheet. British spelling of the noun.

Location.context: Label above the path the drive was mounted at. A noun, not a verb.

Locked.context: A small badge on a row for a drive that has not been opened.

Looking for drives….context: Shown while the first scan runs. Ends with an ellipsis character.

Lúkotta is Finnish for “without a lock”,.context: The paragraph under 'The name' in the About panel, explaining what the app's name means. The Finnish translation deliberately says something else: this sentence exists to explain Finnish to people who do not speak it, and to a Finnish reader it explains their own language to them. Finnish instead notes the grammar in passing and says the author is Estonian and chose Finnish because it sounded better. Written by the author; do not replace it with a translation of the English.

Menu Bar.context: Settings section for the status icon.

Needed.context: A small orange badge on a permission row that has not been granted.

No drives found.context: Title when the scan found nothing to offer. Not "encrypted": the list carries every drive this app can open, encrypted or not.

No new drives found..context: Shown for a few seconds under the drive list after Rescan, when looking again turned up nothing that was not already listed. Not a failure: the scan worked and there was nothing new.

No reason was reported. The details belo.context: A failure sentence for when nothing in the engine's output matched any known reason. Points at the transcript underneath.

Not a format %@ can open..context: A row in the disk list: nothing here recognises this volume.

Not found in this build..context: Shown in place of the third-party notices when the file is missing from the bundle.

OK.context: Button that dismisses the sheet. The standard macOS word.

Open.context: Button, and the main action, for a drive that needs no passphrase. Also the confirm button of the file chooser.

Open %@.context: Menu item in the status menu. Brings the app's window forward.

Open Disk Image.context: The title of the file chooser.

Open Disk Image….context: Menu item. Ends with an ellipsis character because a chooser follows.

Open Drive.context: Title of the sheet, and the menu item that opens it. Title case in English.

Open Drive….context: Menu item. Same rule about the ellipsis.

Open Email.context: Button. Opens a new message with the report in it.

Open Privacy & Security → Full Disk Acce.context: Step 1 of three. Both names are panes in System Settings and must match what the reader's Mac shows. The arrow means: then go to. In a right-to-left language it points the other way.

Open Privacy Settings.context: Button, shown only when the failure was a missing permission. Opens System Settings at the pane that grants it.

Open Read-Only.context: Button. Opens a drive that needs no passphrase without allowing anything to be written.

Open Settings.context: Button on the Full Disk Access row. Opens System Settings at that pane.

Open System Settings.context: Button, and the main action on this screen. Opens System Settings directly at Full Disk Access.

Open an Issue.context: Button. Opens the project's issue tracker in a browser.

Open drives again after restarting.context: The setting that reopens drives at login.

Open encrypted drives on macOS.context: The line under the app's name in the header. What the app is, in one phrase.

Open it read-only to copy files out, or.context: Under the warning that writing to this image format is untested. Two ways to avoid the risk.

Open “%@”.context: Title of the unlock screen for a drive that needs no passphrase.

placeholders.is: the drive or image name, in typographic quotes

Opening a disk image.context: A section heading in the help sheet.

Opening read-only.context: A section heading in the help sheet.

Opening “%@”.context: Title of the screen while a drive is being opened.

placeholders.is: the drive name, in typographic quotes

Passphrase.context: Label above the field for a Linux drive. LUKS calls it a passphrase; keep the distinction from password where the language has one.

Password or recovery key.context: Label above the field for a BitLocker drive, which accepts either.

Permissions.context: A section heading in the help sheet.

Preparing.context: The first step: the workspace and the environment are being made ready. A step name in a list.

Quit.context: Button. Closes the app once it has removed itself.

Quit and leave %lld drives open?.context: Title of the dialogue when quitting with several drives open. Needs the plural forms of this language.

Quit and leave “%@” open?.context: The same dialogue when one drive is open.

placeholders.is: the drive name, in typographic quotes

Quitting….context: A small panel shown while the app is closing, when open drives have to be ejected first and that takes a moment. Present participle, with an ellipsis: the app is going, and has not gone yet.

Raw disk images, and a BitLocker or LUKS.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app can open. A fragment, not a sentence: no full stop.

Read-Only.context: A small badge on a row for a drive opened without write access.

Reading a raw disk and mounting a filesy.context: The explanation on the administrator row. The last sentence matters: the password goes to macOS, not to this app.
The same row when the helper is registered but still waiting for approval in Login Items.

Relaunch.context: Button. Quits and starts the app again, which is what makes a newly granted permission take effect. Step 3 names this button.

Remember this key in my Keychain.context: Checkbox beside the passphrase field. Keychain is Apple's password store.

Removable volumes: requested by macOS th.context: A bullet in the permissions list. Removable volumes is the name macOS gives the permission.

Report This Issue.context: Button. Opens the report sheet with this failure already filled in.

Report a problem.context: Tooltip on the report button in the header.

Report a problem or send a crash report.context: The same tooltip when a crash report was found, so there is more to send.

Report an Issue.context: Title of the sheet, and the menu item that opens it.

Report an Issue….context: Menu item. Same rule about the ellipsis.

Requirements.context: A section heading in the help sheet.

Seeing connected drives.context: Row title for the permission that lets the app see drives that are plugged in.

Set Up.context: Button on the administrator row. Registers the background helper so no password is needed again.

Setting up did not finish. You can try a.context: Shown when installing the background helper did not work -- the password panel was closed, or the daemon would not start. Beside it is a Try Again button. Says plainly that it can be retried rather than leaving somebody stuck.

Setting up the Linux environment.context: Shown once, on first use, while the bundled Linux system is unpacked. Takes a while and has its own percentage.

Setting up….context: The state shown beside the administrator step while the password panel is up and the daemon is being installed. A fragment, with an ellipsis, as macOS writes progress.

Settings.context: Tooltip on the settings button in the header, and the name of that window.

Show.context: Tooltip on the eye button while the typed passphrase is hidden.

Show in Finder.context: Button. Opens a Finder window at the volume that was just mounted.

Show the credential.context: Read aloud for that button in the same state.

Some permissions are still needed.context: Title of the panel listing what macOS still wants. Shown only while something is outstanding.

Source.context: A row label in the About section, linking to the source code.

Specifications.context: The title of the specifications sheet.

Specs.context: A tab or button label leading to the specifications. Short by design.

Switch on Full Disk Access for %@ in the.context: Shown after switching on reopening at login, when the permission is still missing.

System.context: Appearance and language choice: follow the Mac.

That looks like a recovery key, but it h.context: Shown when what was typed is clearly an attempt at a BitLocker recovery key -- only digits, spaces and hyphens -- but the wrong number of digits. A genuine key is 48 digits in 8 groups of 6. The placeholder is how many digits were actually typed.

That password or recovery key did not un.context: Shown under the passphrase field, and as the failure summary, when the credential was refused. The commonest failure there is.

The Full Disk Access list, with an app's.context: Read aloud in place of the screenshot on this screen, for somebody who cannot see it.

The Full Disk Access list, with the + bu.context: Read aloud in place of the other screenshot on this screen.

The Linux environment is unpacked once,.context: Explains why the first open is slower than every one after it.

The Linux environment will be deleted, f.context: A line in the uninstall confirmation. Needs plural forms.

The background helper is not set up, so.context: The body of the quit dialogue when one drive is open and no helper is registered. Two paragraphs separated by a blank line.

The background helper will be unregister.context: A line in the uninstall confirmation.

The drive appears in the Finder sidebar.context: Two lines in an information box. The first says where to find the opened drive; the second is the one instruction that matters, since pulling a drive out without ejecting it can lose data. Locations is the name of a section in Finder's sidebar.

The drive could not be opened..context: The failure summary when nothing more particular is known: the attempt ended, or ran past the time this app waits, and no rule recognised what the engine said. Plain and short on purpose -- whatever the engine wrote is under it, for a report.

The drive is busy. Close anything using.context: A failure sentence: something else on the Mac is holding the drive.

The drive is handed to Finder over a loc.context: Explains why an opened drive looks like a network share. Locations is a section of the Finder sidebar.

The drive stays in Finder after %@ quits.context: The body of the quit dialogue when the helper is registered and one drive is open.

The drive was not opened. %@.context: Said by a screen reader when that screen appears: the title, then the sentence explaining why.

The engine did not recognise a filesyste.context: A failure sentence covering two possibilities at once, since they cannot be told apart from the engine's output.

The engine reported nothing at all. The.context: A failure sentence for silence from the engine.

The language changes when %@ starts agai.context: Shown after choosing a language, since macOS loads a language table at launch.

The name.context: A section heading in the help sheet, above the paragraph about where Lukotta comes from.

The passphrase this drive was encrypted.context: Grey line under the field for a Linux drive.

The password the drive was locked with,.context: Grey line under the field for a BitLocker drive. A recovery key is 48 digits in eight groups.

The virtualisation engine could not star.context: A failure sentence: the small Linux virtual machine would not start.

There is no password to enter..context: Grey line under the note that a drive is not encrypted.

There is nothing in “%@” that %@ can ope.context: Refusal for a file the app read successfully and found nothing openable in.

placeholders.is: the file name, in typographic quotes

Third-Party Notices.context: A row label in the About section, leading to the licences of everything the app carries.

This copy of %@ is incomplete: its Linux.context: The same, for the Linux environment the engine boots. 'Linux' is a protected name and stays as it is. The placeholder is the application's name.

This copy of %@ is incomplete: its drive.context: Shown when the app's own drive engine is not inside the application bundle, which means the copy was damaged or incompletely copied. The placeholder is the application's name.

This drive holds %lld volumes and not al.context: A notice after a container mount where some volumes did not open. Needs the plural forms of this language.

placeholders.is: how many volumes the drive holds

This drive holds an installer disc image.context: Shown when a USB stick still carries an installer disc image. A quick format in Windows or macOS writes inside a partition and leaves the image's own structures at the front of the disk, where both systems keep reading them, so the drive looks unformatted rather than empty. `clean` and Disk Utility's Erase are the names of those commands and are not translated.

This drive holds several volumes inside.context: A failure sentence for a container the app could not take apart. Asks for a report because it is a case worth seeing.

This drive is not encrypted..context: Title of the blue note for a drive that turned out to need no passphrase.

This drive needs repairing, so it will t.context: Replaces "This usually takes under a minute." under the title while a damaged drive is being repaired, because that estimate stops being true. States a fact and gives a reason to wait; it is not an apology and not a warning, and nothing is being lost.

This drive opened read-only: its filesys.context: Shown beside a drive that is open when the system's mount table says it is read-only although writing was asked for -- a filesystem that needs repair, or one a previous machine left mid-transaction. Without it the drive looked writable and the first save failed with the system's own refusal and no explanation.

This file could not be opened just now..context: Shown when the app asked macOS which disk images are attached and got no answer in time, so it would not risk attaching the same file twice. Nothing is wrong with the file itself.

This partition is not a BitLocker volume.context: A failure sentence: the partition type suggested BitLocker and the contents did not.

This usually takes under a minute..context: Reassurance under the progress line, so a wait does not look like a hang.

This version needs setting up again. It.context: Shown when the app has been updated and the background helper on this Mac is the older version. Beside it is a button that sets it up again, which asks for an administrator password once.

Try Again.context: Button, and the default action. Repeats the same attempt unchanged; Back is the way to change anything.

Uninstall.context: Button that starts removing the app.

Uninstall %@….context: Menu item. Same rule about the ellipsis.

Unlock.context: Button, and the main action, for a drive that is encrypted.

Unlock Read-Only.context: The same for opening it without allowing anything to be written.

Unlock this drive.context: Read aloud for a row that can be opened.

Unlock uses it directly. Forget it to ty.context: Grey line under the note that a saved key is being used. Names the Unlock and Forget buttons.

Unlock “%@”.context: Title of the unlock screen for an encrypted drive.

placeholders.is: the drive or image name, in typographic quotes

Unlocked.context: A small badge on a row for a drive that is open.

Unlocked at %@.context: Under an open row: where the volume was mounted.

Unlocking and mounting.context: The middle step, and the long one: the drive is being unlocked and its filesystem mounted. Where nearly every failure happens.

Unregistering the background helper.context: A step while uninstalling: the privileged helper is deregistered from macOS.

Up to %lld drives can stay unlocked at o.context: A line in the requirements list of the About sheet, beside the memory a drive costs. Says how many drives can be unlocked at the same time.

placeholders.is: how many drives can be open at once, twelve

Using the key saved in your Keychain.context: Title of the green note shown when a passphrase was saved earlier.

VDI.context: The name of a disk image format, shown as a label. Never translated, in any script. VirtualBox's format.

VHD.context: The name of a disk image format, shown as a label. Never translated, in any script. Microsoft's older virtual disk.

VHDX.context: The name of a disk image format, shown as a label. Never translated, in any script. Microsoft's newer one, which this app reads and never writes.

VMDK.context: The name of a disk image format, shown as a label. Never translated, in any script. VMware's format.

Version %@ (%@).context: A row in the About section: the version, then the build number in brackets.

Virtual machine disks: qcow2, VMDK, VDI,.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app can open. A fragment, not a sentence: no full stop. Every name in it is a product.

Volumes opened.context: Label above the count, when a container held more than one volume and several were opened.

Waiting for your approval.context: A step shown only when macOS is asking the reader to authorise the operation. Never shown when the background helper is registered.

Was refused. In Files & Folders, switch.context: The explanation on the drives row after the permission was refused. Files and Folders and Removable Volumes are both names on the reader's own Mac.

Website.context: A row label in the About section.

Welcome to %@.context: Title of the permission screen on first use.

What a drive contains is only known once.context: The footnote under the list. Explains why a row says what a drive may be rather than what it is.

What happened.context: Read aloud as the name of the box the reader types into.

What happened?.context: The heading above that box, shown on screen.

What it can open.context: A section heading in the help sheet.

What it cannot open.context: A section heading in the help sheet.

What to do.context: Read aloud as the name of the group holding the three numbered steps. Not shown on screen.

Why it appears as a network drive.context: A section heading in the help sheet.

Windows NTFS drives, including ones Wind.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app can open. A fragment, not a sentence: no full stop.

Windows is part-way through encrypting o.context: A failure sentence: BitLocker is mid-conversion and the drive cannot be opened until Windows finishes.

Writing to this image format is untested.context: Title of the orange note for an image format written by a driver built for this app. It warns about the format, not about the drive inside it.

You can read and write files on it..context: One line under the title of an opened drive. Says what may be done with it now.

You can read files on it. It was opened.context: The same line for a drive opened read-only, either because that was asked for or because writing was refused.

You can still check whenever you like..context: Shown under the updates setting when automatic checking is off.

You cancelled the administrator prompt,.context: Shown after somebody presses Cancel on the macOS administrator password panel that appears when opening a physical drive. Nothing went wrong; it says plainly why the drive did not open.

Your drives are set to open again after.context: Under the title when drives could not be reopened. Says what happened and names the three ordinary causes, so it does not read as a fault.

done.context: Said by a screen reader for a step that has finished. Lower case, read inside a sentence.

ext4, btrfs and XFS filesystems inside t.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of what the app can open. A fragment, not a sentence: no full stop. Filesystem names, never translated.

in progress.context: The same for the step running now.

locked.context: Said by a screen reader as part of a row's description. Lower case: it is read inside a sentence.

macOS 15 Sequoia or later.context: A bullet in the help sheet's list of requirements. A fragment: no full stop. Sequoia is Apple's name for that release.

macOS System Volumes.context: The label of the collapsed group at the foot of the disk list, holding the volumes macOS makes for itself. APFS puts a dozen in every container -- Preboot, Recovery, VM -- and none of them is a thing to open.

macOS already has this drive mounted. Ej.context: A failure sentence: macOS is holding the volume, so the engine cannot have it.

macOS blocked access to the drive. %@ ne.context: A failure sentence for a missing permission. Full Disk Access is the name macOS gives it.

macOS could not open this file as a disk.context: Refusal when macOS itself declined to attach the file.

macOS has this open at %@..context: A row in the disk list: macOS has already mounted this volume, and where.

macOS reads and writes exFAT itself, so.context: Explains why a volume appeared in Finder that this app is not holding: the image needed nothing this app does, so it was handed straight to macOS.

macOS reads this format itself..context: A row in the disk list: nothing is needed from this app for this volume.

macOS reads this format itself. It did n.context: A notice for an image macOS handles, which it declined to mount.

macOS refused %@ access to this drive. S.context: A notice at the top of the unlock screen after the removable-volumes permission was refused. Below means the panel further down this screen.

macOS would not add %@ to your login ite.context: Shown when registering the login item failed. Names three panes in order; use Apple's words for each.

macOS would not let go of this drive. Cl.context: Shown when the button above was pressed and macOS refused to unmount the drive, which normally means a program still has a file open on it.

macOS wrote %@. It is not sent anywhere.context: Under the crash-report note. The file name is a macOS crash log.

not reached.context: Said by a screen reader for a step the mount never got to. Lower case: it is read as part of a sentence, not shown as a label.

qcow2.context: The name of a disk image format, shown as a label. Never translated, in any script. QEMU's format. Always lower case.

qcow2, VMDK, VDI and VHD images can be w.context: A bullet under Opening a disk image.

raw image.context: A disk image with no wrapper at all: the bytes of a disk in a file. The word image is translated; raw may be, where the language has a natural word for unwrapped.

stopped here.context: Marks the step a failed mount stopped at, beside it on the failure screen. Lower case, small.

unlocked.context: The same, for an open drive.

waiting.context: Said by a screen reader for the step in progress. Lower case, read as part of a sentence.

“%@” could not be read..context: Refusal when the file could not be opened at all: permissions, or a file that has gone.

placeholders.is: the file name, in typographic quotes

“%@” had stopped responding and was disc.context: A notice after one drive went away.

placeholders.is: the drive name, in typographic quotes

“%@” holds an encrypted volume, and this.context: Refusal on a build whose engine cannot unlock encryption found inside an image file.

“%@” holds only the changes from another.context: Refusal for a differencing image, which is meaningless without its parent.

“%@” is a VDI, and this build’s drive en.context: Refusal on a build whose engine was assembled without the VDI driver. Not a common case: it means the app was built without the patches.

“%@” is a dynamic VHD, and this build’s.context: The same, for a dynamic VHD. A fixed VHD is a disk with a footer after it and needs no driver.

“%@” is a sparse VMDK, and this build’s.context: The same, for a sparse VMDK. Sparse and flat are the two ways a VMDK stores its data.

“%@” is marked as damaged. Repair it bef.context: Refusal for a qcow2 whose header says it was left in a bad state.

“%@” is not a disk image..context: Refusal when nothing in the file looks like any format the app reads.

“%@” is one of a chain of snapshots. Ope.context: Refusal for a snapshot, which describes changes to another disk rather than a disk.

“%@” is smaller than its footer states,.context: Refusal for a VHD whose footer claims more than the file holds, which usually means a truncated copy.

“%@” is unlocked.context: Title of the screen for a drive that is now open, and said by a screen reader when it appears.

placeholders.is: the drive name, in typographic quotes

“%@” names another file on this Mac, whi.context: Refusal for an image that points at a second file. Opening it would open something the reader did not choose.

“%@” needs “%@”, which is not beside it..context: Refusal for a multi-file image with a piece missing. Two names in one sentence: the image, then the file it wants.

“%@” opened in macOS.context: Title of that sheet. The image was opened by macOS, not by this app; the word order matters, as it is not the app that opened it.

placeholders.is: the file name, in typographic quotes

“%@” was disconnected..context: A notice above the list when a drive went away while it was open.

placeholders.is: the drive name, in typographic quotes

“%@” was not shut down cleanly, and its.context: Refusal for a VHDX with unwritten changes in its log. Only the virtual machine that made it can replay that.
